chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a slave girl was bought for him from Kufa. He said:

So she went to attend to one of the needs, and she said, 'O mother!' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Do you have a mother?' She said, 'Yes'. So he ordered that she be returned, and said: 'I do not feel safe if I were to keep her, from seeing in my children what I dislike.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) return a slave girl he had purchased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s (peace be upon him) sensitivity to familial bonds even within the institution of slavery, illustrating the principle that ownership does not negate kinship ties. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that separating a mother from her child is a source of emotional distress ('what one dislikes') and thus merited compensation or return, reflecting the broader ethical imperative of preserving family integrity in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, a slave girl having been bought for him<sup>asws</sup> from Al-Kufa. So he<sup>asws</sup> went on to stand regarding one of the needs, so she said, ‘O mother!’ So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there a mother for you?’ She said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered with her to be returned, and said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not feel safe if I<sup>asws</sup> were to keep her, from seeing in my<sup>asws</sup> children what I<sup>asws</sup> dislike’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “I once bought a slave-girl from al-Kufah for abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He then went so she can do a certain task. She said, ‘O mother!’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ‘Do you have a mother?’ She replied, ‘Yes, I have a mother.’ He (the Imam) commanded to return her and said, ‘On keeping her I did not feel safe from seeing in my children what I dislike to see.’”
